chunks: From him, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife while she was pregnant, then took her back, then divorced her, then took her back, then divorced her the third time in one day, making her irrevocably divorced from him. He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Does triple divorce in one day count as three separate divorces in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the fiqh of triple talaq pronounced in a single sitting, confirming that three divorces issued to a pregnant wife in one day constitute a final, irrevocable separation (talaq mughallazah). The Imam’s affirmative response underscores the Shia view that the count is valid even if pronounced simultaneously, distinguishing it from the Hanafi 'one talaq' opinion and aligning with the majority of jurists who require the wife to marry another man before remarrying the first husband.
